input.context: The crew plugin must choose a cross-agent state transport mechanism for slice-progress tracking. Three options are on the table: (A) filesystem files (.claude/state/crew/slice-progress.md) read by all agents and the CLI, (B) an in-memory store passed as JSON on stdin to each subagent, (C) a local SQLite database. Evaluate the three options against: inspectability, Windows support, worktree isolation, restart recovery, and implementation overhead.
constraints: Must work across git worktrees (each has own .claude/state/)
Must survive process crash and restart (no in-memory-only state)
Must be readable by human operators without tooling
Node 22.6+ consumer runtime — no extra binaries beyond what ships with Node
Implementation must fit in ≤2 days of builder work

expected_output.summary: Option A (filesystem) wins. Markdown files are human-readable without tooling, git-committable for cross-machine history, naturally worktree-isolated (.claude/state/ is per-tree), and crash-safe (append-only JSONL for events). SQLite adds a native module dependency that complicates Windows CI. In-memory fails restart-recovery.
expected_output.non_goals_explicit: Does not evaluate distributed stores (Redis, Postgres) — out of scope for local-first tool
failure_modes_named: Concurrent writes from parallel builders to same state file — mitigated by per-worktree state isolation (each worktree has own .claude/state/)
State file left in inconsistent state on SIGTERM — mitigated by atomic-swap writes (write to .tmp then rename)
Large state file degrades grep/read performance — mitigated by splitting events into append-only JSONL and keeping summary in short .md

interfaces_typed.SliceProgress: { slice_id: string; status: 'in-progress'|'done'|'blocked'; builder?: string; reviewer?: string; validator?: string; updated_at: string }

expected_output.test_strategy_present: Unit tests for atomic-swap writer; integration test for concurrent writes from 2 process workers
expected_output.tradeoffs_articulated: SQLite: no extra binary on Windows if using better-sqlite3 (native module) — BUT native modules complicate Bun/Node parity and CI matrix. Filesystem is the pragmatic baseline; SQLite is a future upgrade path if query complexity grows.

notes: Mined from crew constitution memory model + deployment.md file-state design. Real choice: filesystem (Option A) was shipped. Seed type: tradeoff_matrix.
